output.summary: Approved G1038 design revision 3 after three review rounds (round 3 approved, all prior findings resolved). Goal branches sync with trunk by merge commits (git merge-tree with the old base_commit as merge base; fast-forward pushes only; conflicts checked out for resolution and never redone), behind capability merge_sync as a precondition, with merge mode sticky per branch. Tests vs implementation are split by recorded frozen paths and per-phase submit ranges, so test fixes may follow implementation commits without rewrites. Integrate squashes to a `test:` commit and an implementation commit (type ranked from release.config.cjs) on the last synced base, with the PR head always the newest commit. Conventional commits enforced on work branches, PR titles and trunk merge commits; goal-ref record commits keep machine subjects. Notes for implement: take the squash body's parent only when above base_commit; mention merge-queue message settings in REPAIR.

output.summary: Revision 3 builds on revision 2 and fixes only the three open round-2 items. The conflict resume compares the worktree with the conflicted tree T (git diff --name-only T plus ls-files --others), not git status against HEAD, and builds the merge from the listed files in a temporary index (verified on Git 2.55.0). Conventional commits now also cover the PR title (c2's subject) and the trunk commit that the merge op writes: squash gets c2's subject and the bodies, merge gets chore(merge): G<g> <title> (#<pr>), rebase gets nothing. Merge mode is sticky per work branch: without merge_sync in the policy, a branch that has sync merges blocks base with a policy item instead of being rebased, and removing merge_sync while such branches are open is documented as unsupported.

findings.response: fixed: the resume (4.2) refuses when git status --untracked-files=all shows any path outside the listed files (re-blocks listing them), and then stages only the listed files with git add -A --literal-pathspecs -- <files>. findings.text: The conflict resume (§4.2) runs 'git add -A', so anything in the worktree goes into the merge commit, and from there into the goal's code and its squashed PR: untracked scratch files, *.orig files from mergetool, build output, edits to files that did not conflict. Fix: stage only the listed files (git add -A -- <files>); re-block if any other path differs from T, listing those paths, and refuse untracked or modified files outside the list. Cover this in test 1.

findings.response: fixed: adopted the owner's decision, recorded verbatim in 2.1, in 4.8 and D10. Covered: every commit on work, stack and PR branches, agent- and engine-made. Exempt: record commits on goal refs (zzzops: answer G<g> ..., parsed by G1026) and lease refs, because they are machine-parsed and never reach trunk. Submit refuses non-conventional subjects (commit_subject) and non-test commits from the preserved node (test_commit_type), and implement commits touching frozen paths (test_freeze, now per commit); codes, texts and the SPEC §4.14 text are given. Engine subjects become chore(sync): merge <onto> into G<g> and chore(stack): combine/partial combine for G<g>; integrate's commits are test: and the derived type (4.5.2). Test 10 covers both refusals and the engine subjects; test 5 covers the type derivation.
findings.text: Owner decision, relayed by the root (material). Owner, verbatim: "Yeah, we should ensure we always use conventional commit messages". This was in reply to the root's proposal: keep the tests/implementation split by recorded frozen paths and per-phase submit ranges, not by commit message; (1) submit refuses commits whose subjects are not conventional commits, test_design's commits must be test:, and implement's commits must not touch frozen paths; (2) integrate's squashed tests commit is 'test: ...' and the implementation commit's type is derived from the goal's commits. The design must adopt this and state which commits the rule covers. The root recommends: every commit on work and PR branches, agent-made and engine-made (docs(review): commits already comply); engine record commits on goal refs ('zzzops: answer G<g> ...', which G1026 parses) keep their machine subjects because they never reach trunk; justify any other scope. G1038's own engine commits do not comply: the sync merge 'Merge <onto> into zzzops/work/g<g> (zzzops base)' (§4.1), and the combine commits 'zzzops: stack for G<g> ...' / 'zzzops: partial stack' (base.py combine) on the stack branches PRs target. Give them conventional subjects (for example chore(sync): ..., chore(stack): ...) or exclude them with a reason. Add the submit refusal codes and texts, the SPEC §4.14 text, tests for both refusals and for the engine subjects, and the type derivation from the implementation commits' conventional types.

Still open on review_design:1:6: the 4.2 resume check 2 (`git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` lists no path outside the listed files) always re-blocks. After `git read-tree -u --reset T` the index is T and HEAD stays at the tip, so status reports every path where T differs from the tip (every trunk-side change) as a staged modification. Verified on Git 2.55.0: trunk changes a.txt and t.txt, the goal changes a.txt; after read-tree and editing a.txt, status prints `MM a.txt` and `M  t.txt`, while `git diff --name-only T` prints only a.txt. Fix: compare against T: `git diff --name-only -z T --` (worktree vs T, whatever the agent staged) plus `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` for untracked paths, and refuse any path outside the listed files. Add a test-1 case where trunk also changes a non-conflicting file and the resume is accepted.

Still open on review_design:1:7, one residual: D10 and 4.8 justify the scope with 'these are the only branches whose commits reach trunk', which is false. The merge op runs `gh pr merge --<method>` (merge.py:92), which writes a trunk commit whose subject is the PR title, not a conventional subject. dev's tip f4eaf74 'Replace ENGINE_VERSION and engine.min with declared engine capabilities (G1027) (#759)' is one. Under merge.method `merge` this adds a non-conventional commit per goal to dev and main, against the owner's 'always'. Under `squash`, which the policy allows and section 3 mentions, GitHub writes one commit titled with the PR title, so semantic-release sees no conventional commit and c2's derived type and release are lost, which breaks the 4.5.2 claim. Fix: the merge op passes --subject/--body to gh pr merge: for squash, c2's subject and a body with c1's and c2's bodies and the breaking footers; for merge, a conventional subject such as `chore(merge): <PR title> (#n)`; for rebase, nothing. Add this to 4.8's covered list, SPEC §4.14/§5.5 and a test-10 case per method, or exempt trunk merge commits with a true reason and still fix the squash case.

N1: D9's 'no older engine can ever see a merge-synced branch' fails on the documented rollback. SPEC's upgrade procedure at f4eaf74 says 'Rollback is the same procedure removing the names'. Once merge_sync is removed from settings.engine.requires, the new engine's mode becomes rebase (4.1) and older engines un-pause, and both run today's `rebase -q --onto onto old` on a work branch with chore(sync): merges: the merges are dropped, every resolved conflict is redone and the branch is force-pushed. That is the review_design:1:5 hazard again. Fix: make merge mode sticky per branch. If W's first-parent history above base_commit has an engine sync merge and the policy does not require merge_sync, base blocks with a policy item ('the work branch has merge syncs; the policy must require merge_sync') and pushes nothing. merge_sync.txt and SPEC §4.5/§8 state that removing merge_sync is not supported while an open goal's work branch has merge syncs. Add a test-8 case.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Two pieces of machinery caused most of the friction in the G1022–G1028 run:
- Syncing a goal with the integration branch is a rebase. Conflict resolutions are not kept, so each later rebase redoes them, and a rebase rewrites the work branch.
- The frozen tests are the diff up to the tests checkpoint, and the implementation is everything after it, so a test fix found after implement has to be inserted before the implementation commits. That needs a history rewrite and a force-push of the work branch, which only the owner could run. It happened four times (G1025, G1026, G1027 twice).

Owner decisions (verbatim):
- "For updating the branch with the trunk, I think merges might work better as conflict resolution doesn't get lost. Then maybe a final rebase when integrating in order to clean up the history?"
- On the integrate history, the owner chose "Squash to tests + code" over rebasing with reused resolutions or keeping the merges: integrate collapses the goal into two commits (tests, implementation) on the trunk tip.
- "I think we may as well get these done now, before dogfooding again"

Scope:
- `base` (and any scheduled sync) brings trunk into the goal's work branch with a merge commit, never a rebase or force-push. A conflicting merge becomes a base finding as G1021 does today.
- test_design may add tests commits after implementation commits. Which tests are frozen, and which diff is the implementation, are computed from paths and checkpoints rather than commit order, so no history rewrite is ever needed during a goal.
- integrate produces the PR branch as exactly two commits on the integration tip: the goal's tests and its implementation (plus the review records the engine already carries, if they must stay separate). The work branch is left as is.
- No owner-run force-push is needed at any point in a goal's normal flow.

Acceptance:
- A goal whose trunk moves twice during delivery syncs by two merges; the second sync does not redo the first sync's conflict resolution.
- A test fix submitted by test_design after implement committed is accepted without any rewrite; implement may not edit it; review_impl sees only implementation changes.
- The PR for such a goal has exactly the tests commit and the implementation commit on the trunk tip, and its tree equals the work branch merged with trunk.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: Sync goal branches with trunk by merge, squash at integrate, and let test fixes land after implementation
